what: Hook strength constraints by event type: UserPromptSubmit MUST be soft (additionalContext), never blocking — blocking rejects the user's message entirely so the agent never sees it. Stop and PreCompact can be blocking safely (Stop has stop_hook_active guard, PreCompact blocks before context loss). PreToolUse(Read) can block with session-scoped tracking to prevent infinite loops. PreToolUse on MCP tools (e.g. aide_recall) should be passthrough (just track, don't block).
why: UserPromptSubmit was changed to blocking and it broke all user prompts matching correction patterns — user couldn't type at all. Blocking on UserPromptSubmit blocks the user's INPUT, not the agent's output. Fundamentally different from Stop/PreCompact which block agent actions.
